mathematics_checks: On uncountable Omega, no set is simultaneously countable and co-countable. The declared measurable sets form a sigma-algebra: complements preserve the class, and a countable union is countable if all members are countable, otherwise it is co-countable. For pairwise disjoint measurable B_n, at most one can be co-countable; if one is, the union has mass one and every other member has mass zero; if none is, the union and the sum both have mass zero. Thus the proposed 0/1 assignment is countably additive with mu(Omega)=1 and mu(empty)=0.

For each x, K(x,.) is the Dirac probability measure at x and L(x,.) is mu. For each fixed measurable B, x maps to K(x,B) is the measurable indicator of B and x maps to L(x,B) is constant. These are precisely the separate kernel requirements. Joint measurability of the diagonal in Omega times Omega is not required or used.

For a countable B, the equality K(x,B)=L(x,B) fails only on B; for co-countable B, it fails only on the countable complement. Each exceptional set is measurable and mu-null, proving forall measurable B, almost everywhere equality, with an event-dependent exception.

For every x the measurable singleton {x} has mu-mass zero but K(x,{x})=1. Consequently the set of x satisfying equality for every measurable event is empty, so the almost-everywhere universal-event statement fails. This is an uncountable-union obstruction, not a failure of closure under countable null unions.

For each measurable B, (mu K)(B)=integral 1_B dmu=mu(B), while (mu L)(B)=integral mu(B) dmu=mu(B) because mu is a probability measure. Both output laws are therefore exactly mu. The example refutes the quantifier interchange and common almost-everywhere equality of kernel measures, not equality of these averaged laws.

If a countable family generated this sigma-algebra, the union C of the countable side of each generator would be countable. Every generator, and hence every set in its generated sigma-algebra, is either all or none on Omega minus C. That remainder has at least two points, whose singleton is measurable in the full sigma-algebra but cannot belong to the generated one. The output is not countably generated; the input type is uncountable. Standard-Borel outputs are countably generated and are outside this counterexample.
